appliesToWhy: census.json pose prone: lying_leg_curl and superman. GA 3.2 also names chest_supported_row and a chest-pad T-bar; the verified chest_supported_row card draws a seated chest-pad row (ACE) and t_bar_row draws the free-standing landmine row, so neither lies face down and both are left out.

checkpoints.label: Hips on the pad
checkpoints.detail: Front of the hips stays pressed against the pad; stop the curl before the hips lift.

checkpoints.label: Neck in line
checkpoints.detail: Head and neck stay neutral, eyes down; do not lift the head.

claims.text: On the lying leg curl keep the front of the hips against the pad; stop the curl before the hips begin to lift, and if the load pulls the pelvis off the bench, reduce the weight or stop slightly earlier.

quotes.text: Hold the handles, gently tighten your abs, and keep the front of your hips in contact with the pad.
quotes.where: How to Do the Lying Leg Curl, 2. Brace before you curl

quotes.text: Stop when you reach the end of your controlled range or before your hips begin to lift.
quotes.where: How to Do the Lying Leg Curl, 3. Curl through your available range

quotes.text: If the load pulls your pelvis off the bench, reduce the weight or stop the curl slightly earlier. Lifting the hips changes the position of the hamstrings and often introduces lower-back movement that does not help the target action.

claims.text: Lifting the hips off the pad is a common lying leg curl mistake; keep the hips pressed against the pad and avoid arching the back.

quotes.text: Curl the Legs: Bend your knees to lift the weighted lever towards your glutes. Keep your hips pressed against the pad.
Slowly exhale and contract your hamstrings, flexing (bending) the knees and moving the resistance pad i na controlled manner towards your butt. Avoid arching your back during this movement.

claims.text: In the superman hold keep a neutral head and neck by looking down at the ground; the head or neck moving out of line is a fault, cued with "eyes down".

quotes.text: Keep neutral head/neck position throughout the exercise by looking down at the ground
Head/neck to moving out of neutral line

claims.text: Keep the neck neutral in the superman; lifting the head too high is a common mistake that strains the neck.

quotes.text: Keep your neck in a neutral position; avoid straining it.
Avoid lifting your head too high to prevent neck strain.

sources.title: Lying Leg Curl: Muscles Worked, Form, and Variations (FitnessVolt)

Bodyweight Superman - How To, Muscles Worked & Form Guide (Liftosaur)

gaps: Neck in line on the lying leg curl: no source read gives a head or neck rule for it (ACE covers the low back only). The checkpoint is not applied there until sourced.
Hips on the floor for the superman: not a rule (the legs lift); no source read gives a hip checkpoint for it.
notes: GA 3.2 named "Hips stay on the pad" and "Neck in line" as the two prone checkpoints with no source; each is now sourced for one exercise only (checkpoint appliesTo).

ACE lying hamstrings curl (GA's first place to check) was read in full on 2026-10-01: it says to brace and avoid arching the back but not to keep the hips down, so FitnessVolt (updated by an ACE-certified trainer, 2026) and Liftosaur carry the hip rule.
